# 什么是 AI 爬虫？

- 原标题：What Is AI Crawler?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-14
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

AI 爬虫是一种自动化机器人，会抓取网页，为大语言模型建立训练数据，或为 AI 生成的答案检索实时内容。与 Googlebot 等传统搜索索引爬虫不同，它的目标是向 AI 系统提供内容。网站所有者可以通过 robots.txt 中的 user-agent 指令控制其访问权限。

### 核心要点

- AI 爬虫分为两类任务：**训练爬虫**收集文本，用于模型预训练，例如 GPTBot、ClaudeBot 和 Bytespider；**检索爬虫**抓取实时网页，回答用户的问题，例如 OAI-SearchBot、PerplexityBot 和 ChatGPT-User。
- 在 robots.txt 中，它们由**各自命名的 user-agent 标识符**控制，与 Googlebot 分开。屏蔽搜索爬虫不等于屏蔽 AI；禁止 AI 训练，也不等于从 AI 答案中退出。
- 某些控制项是策略标识符，而非实际抓取程序。**Google-Extended** 和 **Applebot-Extended** 自己从不抓取网页，只表示已经抓取的内容是否可以用于 AI 训练。
- 并非所有 AI 爬虫都遵守规则。信誉良好的爬虫会遵守 robots.txt；大量记录显示 **Bytespider** 会忽略它。因此，robots.txt 中的一行指令是一项请求，而不是一把锁。

### AI 爬虫如何运作

AI 爬虫的起点与其他机器人相同：通过 HTTP 请求一个网址，读取返回的 HTML。不同的是抓取目的，以及内容最终被送往何处。传统搜索爬虫把读到的内容放进有排名的索引，通过链接回答查询。AI 爬虫则会把文本送进塑造模型权重的训练语料库，或者把刚抓到的网页交给正在为用户[基于资料生成答案](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding/)的模型。

训练与检索的区别，是理解这些机器人的最重要一点。**训练爬虫**会大范围扫描并储存发现的内容，可能在几个月后用于大语言模型的预训练。**检索爬虫**按需抓取，通常是因为用户提出了一个模型希望寻找实时来源的问题；它抓到的页面可能在几秒钟后就被答案引用。同一家公司往往会同时运营这两类爬虫。

每个守规矩的 AI 爬虫都会通过 **user-agent 标识符**表明身份，并在抓取前检查你的 `robots.txt` 中是否有匹配规则。这与管理 Googlebot 的《机器人排除协议》相同，但标识符不同，而且彼此独立。针对 `Googlebot` 的规则不涉及 `GPTBot`。这种独立性正是它的价值所在：你可以让网站完整地收录在 Google 搜索中，同时选择不进入某个 AI 模型的训练集，反过来也可以。如果你希望发布一份机器可读的声明，说明 AI 系统可以使用哪些内容，新兴的 [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) 约定正是为此与 robots.txt 并列存在。

问题在于，robots.txt 指令是一项请求，不是一堵墙。信誉良好的运营方会遵守，另一些则被发现无视这些指令。因此，对于那些与你的风险容忍度最相关的爬虫，服务器层面的封锁才是唯一真正有效的强制措施。

### 常见 AI 爬虫及其 User-Agent

以下均是真实存在、目前有文档记录的 AI 爬虫，以及其运营方公布的精确 robots.txt user-agent 标识符。其中 Google-Extended 和 Applebot-Extended 是控制标识符，本身从不抓取网页。

- **GPTBot**（OpenAI）：标识符为 `GPTBot`。这是训练爬虫，收集内容以改进 OpenAI 的基础模型。完整 UA：`Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`。
- **OAI-SearchBot**（OpenAI）：标识符为 `OAI-SearchBot`。这是检索爬虫，使网站出现在 ChatGPT 的搜索功能中，不用于模型训练。
- **ChatGPT-User**（OpenAI）：标识符为 `ChatGPT-User`。当 ChatGPT 用户或自定义 GPT 明确要求访问某个网页时抓取该页面，不会自动爬取。
- **Google-Extended**（Google）：标识符为 `Google-Extended`。这是一个**没有独立 user-agent** 的 robots.txt 控制标识符，管理 Google 是否可以把已抓取的内容用于训练 Gemini，以及在 Gemini Apps 和 Vertex AI 中作为回答依据。它不影响搜索排名或收录。
- **ClaudeBot**（Anthropic）：标识符为 `ClaudeBot`。这是收集公开网页数据、用于模型开发的训练爬虫。Anthropic 还运营各有独立标识符的 `Claude-User`（用户指示的抓取）和 `Claude-SearchBot`（搜索索引）。
- **PerplexityBot**（Perplexity）：标识符为 `PerplexityBot`。它为网页建立索引，使其可以被 Perplexity 的答案引用。Perplexity 表示，它不用于训练基础模型；实时、由用户触发的浏览则由 `Perplexity-User` 处理。
- **Amazonbot**（Amazon）：标识符为 `Amazonbot`。它抓取网页以改善 Amazon 的产品和服务，也可能用于训练 Amazon 的 AI 模型。它遵守 robots.txt 和页面层面的 `noindex`／`noarchive` 指令。
- **Applebot-Extended**（Apple）：标识符为 `Applebot-Extended`。与 Google-Extended 一样，它不执行爬取，只表示 Applebot 已收录的内容能否用于训练 Apple Intelligence 背后的 Apple 基础模型。
- **Bytespider**（字节跳动）：标识符为 `Bytespider`。这是向字节跳动模型提供内容的训练爬虫。大量记录表明它会忽略 robots.txt，因此，仅靠 Disallow 规则无法可靠地阻止它。

### AI 爬虫示例

最清楚的实际示例是 OpenAI 的训练爬虫 **GPTBot**。GPTBot 来访时，服务器日志会显示 user-agent 字符串为 `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot` 的请求。末尾的 `+https://openai.com/gptbot` 自我介绍链接是一个识别线索：信誉良好的 AI 爬虫会指向说明文档，方便你验证它是否名副其实。

在抓取页面之前，GPTBot 会检查 `robots.txt`，寻找针对其标识符的规则。如果你不希望自己的内容进入 OpenAI 基础模型的训练数据，可以使用以下两行受支持的退出指令：

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /
```

团队容易漏掉的是：这条规则只阻止*训练*爬虫，不影响其他任何机器人。OpenAI 的*检索*爬虫 `OAI-SearchBot` 有自己的标识符，不受禁止 GPTBot 的规则影响。因此，网站完全可以通过禁止 `GPTBot`、同时允许 `OAI-SearchBot`，明确表达“不要用我的内容训练，但可以在 ChatGPT 搜索里引用我”。两种机器人确实在执行不同的任务，OpenAI 之所以分别记录它们，正是为了让你能够分开决策。你也可以验证自称 GPTBot 的请求是否真实：OpenAI 公布了爬虫 IP 范围，如果一个声称自己是 GPTBot 的请求来自范围外的 IP，它就是冒充者，而非真正的爬虫。

### 人们容易搞错的地方

2024 年，大家的条件反射是在 robots.txt 中屏蔽所有 AI 爬虫，理由是“免得它们偷走我们的内容”。我看着网站这样操作，然后六个月后困惑于自己为什么从 ChatGPT 和 Perplexity 的答案中消失。错误在于，把表格里的一行当成了一项统一决策。训练爬虫（GPTBot、ClaudeBot）与检索爬虫（OAI-SearchBot、PerplexityBot）是不同的机器人，使用不同的 user-agent；屏蔽前者不影响后者，而屏蔽后者，会悄悄把你从那些真正希望出现的答案里删除。应该逐个机器人、逐项任务做决定。如果想退出训练，又保留被引用的机会，就禁止 GPTBot、允许 OAI-SearchBot。这是一种受支持的配置，并不矛盾。

### AI 爬虫与搜索爬虫

两者都是通过 HTTP 抓取网页的自动化机器人，也都会读取 `robots.txt`。区别在于它们如何处理读到的内容，而这个区别会改变你对待它们的方式。

|  | AI 爬虫 | 搜索爬虫 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **主要目标** | 训练模型，或为 AI 答案抓取实时内容 | 建立带排名的链接索引 |
| **内容去向** | 训练语料库或 AI 生成的答案 | 返回网址的搜索索引 |
| **机器人示例** | GPTBot、ClaudeBot、PerplexityBot、OAI-SearchBot | Googlebot、Bingbot |
| **robots.txt 标识符** | 各机器人独立命名（`GPTBot`、`ClaudeBot` 等） | `Googlebot`、`Bingbot` |
| **屏蔽的代价** | 被排除在 AI 训练和／或 [AI 答案](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/)之外 | 被排除在自然搜索结果之外 |
| **发布者的成功表现** | 在 AI 答案中被引用 | 作为链接获得排名 |

它们与其说是竞争对手，不如说是从同一扇门进入的两类访客。被 Googlebot 屏蔽的页面会从搜索中消失；被检索爬虫屏蔽的页面会从 AI 答案中消失。由于 AI 答案越来越多地位于蓝色链接之上，甚至取代蓝色链接，发布者现在也应该像一直对待 Googlebot 那样，对检索爬虫本能地“敞开大门”。这正是[生成式引擎优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/)的基本前提。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是 AI 爬虫？

AI 爬虫是自动抓取网页的机器人，用于建立大语言模型的训练数据，或为 AI 生成的答案检索实时内容。它不同于 Googlebot 等传统搜索爬虫，后者的任务是建立带排名的搜索索引。

#### 如何屏蔽 AI 爬虫？

在 robots.txt 中加入爬虫的 user-agent 标识符与 Disallow 规则，例如先写 User-agent: GPTBot，再写 Disallow: /。每个机器人都有自己的标识符，因此需要分别屏蔽。信誉良好的爬虫会遵守这些规则；但有记录显示，Bytespider 等爬虫会完全忽略 robots.txt。

#### 屏蔽 AI 爬虫会让我从 AI 搜索答案中消失吗？

有可能。屏蔽 GPTBot 这类训练爬虫，只影响模型训练。屏蔽 OAI-SearchBot 或 PerplexityBot 这类检索爬虫，则会阻止这些引擎抓取并引用你的实时页面，从而使你退出其答案。它们使用不同的标识符，应分别决策。

#### Google-Extended 是 AI 爬虫吗？

从抓取行为的意义上说，不是。Google-Extended 没有独立爬虫，也从不请求网页。它是 robots.txt 中的控制标识符，告诉 Google 已抓取的内容能否用于训练 Gemini，以及在 Vertex AI 中作为回答依据。Applebot-Extended 的工作方式相同。

### 结论

AI 爬虫向 AI 系统提供内容，而不是建立蓝色链接索引；它会通过一个具名 user-agent 表明身份，你可以允许或禁止其访问。应把爬虫清单视为一组独立选择：如果必须，可以拒绝训练爬虫，但应让检索爬虫进来，因为正是这些机器人决定了 AI 答案是否有机会引用你。

## 英文原文

An AI crawler is an automated bot that fetches web pages to build training data for large language models or to retrieve live content for AI-generated answers. Unlike classic search-index crawlers such as Googlebot, its goal is feeding AI systems, and site owners control its access through robots.txt user-agent directives.

### Key Takeaways

- AI crawlers split into two jobs: **training crawlers** that harvest text for model pre-training (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Bytespider) and **retrieval crawlers** that fetch live pages to answer a user’s question (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, ChatGPT-User).
- They are governed in robots.txt by a **named user-agent token**, separately from Googlebot. Blocking search does not block AI, and blocking AI training does not remove you from AI answers.
- Some controls are policy tokens, not fetchers. **Google-Extended** and **Applebot-Extended** never crawl a page themselves — they only signal whether already-crawled content may be used for AI training.
- Not every AI crawler obeys the rules. Reputable ones honor robots.txt; **Bytespider** has been widely documented ignoring it, so a robots.txt line is a request, not a lock.

### How AI Crawlers Work

An AI crawler starts the same way any bot does: it requests a URL over HTTP and reads the HTML that comes back. What differs is the purpose of the fetch and where the content ends up. A classic search crawler files what it reads into a ranked index that answers queries with links. An AI crawler either pipes the text into a training corpus that shapes a model’s weights, or hands the freshly fetched page to a model that is [grounding](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding/) an answer for a user right now.

That split — training versus retrieval — is the single most important thing to understand about these bots. A **training crawler** sweeps broadly and stores what it finds so it can be used to pre-train a large language model months later. A **retrieval crawler** fetches on demand, usually because a user asked a question the model wants live sources for, and the page it grabs may be quoted in the answer seconds afterward. The same company often runs one of each.

Every well-behaved AI crawler identifies itself with a **user-agent token** and looks for a matching rule in your `robots.txt` before it fetches. This is the same Robots Exclusion Protocol that governs Googlebot, but the tokens are different and independent. A rule for `Googlebot` says nothing about `GPTBot`. That independence is the feature: you can stay fully indexed in Google Search while opting out of one AI model’s training set, or vice versa. If you want to publish a machine-readable statement of what AI systems may use, the emerging [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) convention sits alongside robots.txt for exactly this purpose.

The catch is that a robots.txt directive is a request, not a wall. Reputable operators honor it. Others have been caught ignoring it, which means for the crawlers that matter most to your risk tolerance, server-level blocking is the only enforcement that actually holds.

### Named AI Crawlers and Their User-Agents

These are real, currently documented AI crawlers and the exact robots.txt user-agent tokens their operators publish. Two of them — Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended — are control tokens that never fetch a page themselves.

- **GPTBot** (OpenAI) — token `GPTBot`. A training crawler that collects content to improve OpenAI’s foundation models. Full UA: `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`.
- **OAI-SearchBot** (OpenAI) — token `OAI-SearchBot`. A retrieval crawler that surfaces sites inside ChatGPT’s search features. Not used for model training.
- **ChatGPT-User** (OpenAI) — token `ChatGPT-User`. Fetches a page when a ChatGPT user or a Custom GPT explicitly asks to visit it. It does not crawl automatically.
- **Google-Extended** (Google) — token `Google-Extended`. A robots.txt control token with **no separate user-agent**; it governs whether Google may use already-crawled content to train Gemini and for grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. It does not affect Search ranking or inclusion.
- **ClaudeBot** (Anthropic) — token `ClaudeBot`. A training crawler gathering public web data for model development. Anthropic also runs `Claude-User` (user-directed fetches) and `Claude-SearchBot` (search indexing) under their own tokens.
- **PerplexityBot** (Perplexity) — token `PerplexityBot`. Indexes pages so they can be cited in Perplexity answers. Perplexity states it is not used to train foundation models; `Perplexity-User` handles live, user-triggered browsing.
- **Amazonbot** (Amazon) — token `Amazonbot`. Crawls to improve Amazon products and services and may be used to train Amazon’s AI models. Respects robots.txt and page-level `noindex`/`noarchive`.
- **Applebot-Extended** (Apple) — token `Applebot-Extended`. Like Google-Extended, it does not crawl; it signals whether content already indexed by Applebot may be used to train Apple’s foundation models behind Apple Intelligence.
- **Bytespider** (ByteDance) — token `Bytespider`. A training crawler feeding ByteDance’s models. Widely documented ignoring robots.txt, so a Disallow rule alone will not reliably stop it.

### Example of an AI Crawler

The clearest worked example is **GPTBot**, OpenAI’s training crawler. When GPTBot visits, your server log shows a request with the user-agent string `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`. That `+https://openai.com/gptbot` self-link is the tell: reputable AI crawlers point to a documentation page so you can verify the bot is what it claims.

Before fetching your pages, GPTBot checks `robots.txt` for a rule addressed to its token. If you want to keep your content out of OpenAI’s foundation-model training data, the supported opt-out is two lines:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /
```

Here is the part teams miss. That rule stops the *training* crawler and nothing else. OpenAI’s *retrieval* crawler, `OAI-SearchBot`, has its own token and is unaffected by a GPTBot disallow. So a site can legitimately say “do not train on me, but do cite me in ChatGPT search” by disallowing `GPTBot` while leaving `OAI-SearchBot` allowed. The two bots do genuinely different jobs, and OpenAI documents them as separate precisely so you can make that split decision. Verifying GPTBot is honest is also possible: OpenAI publishes its crawler IP ranges, so a request claiming to be GPTBot from an IP outside that range is an impostor, not the real bot.

### The thing people get wrong

The reflex move in 2024 was to block every AI crawler in robots.txt "before they steal our content." I watched sites do this and then wonder why they vanished from ChatGPT and Perplexity answers six months later. The mistake is treating one row in a table as one decision. Training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) and retrieval crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) are different bots with different user-agents, and blocking the first does nothing to the second while blocking the second quietly deletes you from the answers you actually want to appear in. Decide per bot, per job. If you want to opt out of training but stay citable, disallow GPTBot and allow OAI-SearchBot — that is a supported configuration, not a contradiction.

### AI Crawler vs Search Crawler

Both are automated bots that fetch pages over HTTP and both read `robots.txt`. The difference is what they do with what they read — and that difference changes how you should treat them.

|  | AI Crawler | Search Crawler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Primary goal** | Train a model or fetch live content for an AI answer | Build a ranked index of links |
| **Where content goes** | A training corpus or an AI-generated answer | A search index that returns URLs |
| **Example bots** | GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot | Googlebot, Bingbot |
| **robots.txt token** | Named per bot (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, …) | `Googlebot`, `Bingbot` |
| **What blocking costs you** | Exclusion from AI training and/or [AI answers](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) | Exclusion from organic search results |
| **Success for the publisher** | Being cited inside an AI answer | Ranking as a link |

They are not rivals so much as two audiences arriving through the same door. A page you block from Googlebot disappears from search; a page you block from the retrieval crawlers disappears from AI answers. Because AI answers increasingly sit above or in place of the blue links, the retrieval crawlers now deserve the same “keep the door open” instinct that publishers have always extended to Googlebot — which is the whole premise of [generative engine optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/).

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is an AI crawler?

An AI crawler is an automated bot that fetches web pages to build training data for a large language model or to retrieve live content for an AI-generated answer. It is distinct from a classic search crawler like Googlebot, whose job is to build a ranked search index.

#### How do I block AI crawlers?

Add the crawler’s named user-agent token to robots.txt with a Disallow rule — for example, User-agent: GPTBot then Disallow: /. Each bot has its own token, so you block them individually. Reputable crawlers honor this; some, like Bytespider, have been documented ignoring robots.txt entirely.

#### Does blocking an AI crawler remove me from AI search answers?

It can. Blocking a training crawler like GPTBot only affects model training. Blocking a retrieval crawler like OAI-SearchBot or PerplexityBot stops those engines from fetching and citing your live pages, which removes you from their answers. They are separate tokens and separate decisions.

#### Is Google-Extended an AI crawler?

No, not in the fetching sense. Google-Extended has no separate crawler and never requests a page. It is a robots.txt control token that tells Google whether content it already crawled may be used to train Gemini and for grounding in Vertex AI. Applebot-Extended works the same way.

### The Bottom Line

An AI crawler feeds AI systems, not a blue-link index, and it announces itself with a named user-agent you can allow or disallow. Treat the crawler list as a set of independent choices: keep training crawlers out if you must, but let the retrieval crawlers in, because those are the bots that decide whether an AI answer can cite you at all.
